content: Methyldopa functions by relaxing blood vessels, which facilitates smoother blood flow throughout the body. This combination medication may also be used for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional details. This medication is available in tablet form and is taken orally, typically two or three times daily. Follow the instructions on your prescription label precisely, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take methyldopa and hydrochlorothiazide exactly as prescribed. Do not alter the dosage or frequency without consulting your doctor. Continue taking it even if you feel well, and do not stop without first discussing it with your doctor. Before starting methyldopa and hydrochlorothiazide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to methyldopa, hydrochlorothiazide, sulfa drugs, or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially cholestyramine, digoxin, haloperidol, levodopa, lithium, MAO inhibitors, diabetes medications, prednisone, probenecid, tolbutamide, and vitamins. Avoid taking this medication with iron supplements or vitamins containing iron. Notify your doctor if you have a history of kidney or liver disease, diabetes, gout, or high cholesterol. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. Should you become pregnant while on this medication, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking methyldopa and hydrochlorothiazide. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery for 48-72 hours after starting the medication or after a dosage increase. Consult your doctor about the safe use of alcohol, as it may exacerbate the side effects of this medication. Your doctor may recommend a low-salt or low-sodium diet while you are taking this medication. Follow these dietary instructions carefully. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Methyldopa and hydrochlorothiazide may cause side effects. A harmless but notable effect is the darkening of urine when exposed to air. Common side effects include frequent urination, dry mouth, drowsiness, headache, upset stomach, vomiting, loss of appetite, diarrhea, gas, and rash. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects require immediate medical attention. These include extreme fatigue, muscle weakness or cramps, unexplained fever, yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), difficulty breathing, and swelling of the ankles or feet. If you experience a severe reaction, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store this medication in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly; consult your pharmacist for guidance. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. To alleviate dry mouth caused by this medication, chew gum or suck on sugarless hard candy. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. This medication is also sold under the brand name Aldoril®.
